summary: Orchestrator state serializer drift causing SLA cohort aggregation mismatch in weekly reports
description:
Issue summary:
Orchestrator process that serializes routing/template binding state has begun emitting cohort identifiers with a transient prefix ("tmp_cohort:") which the nightly aggregation job does not normalize. This caused the weekly SLA/cohort report to undercount P1 SLAs and misattribute escalations to an empty cohort bucket.

Impact:
- Incorrect SLA cohort counts in weekly executive report for 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-28 window.
- Automated routing tests flagged ~12% of incidents as "unmatched cohort" leading to noisy reroutes and temporary owner-flapping.
- Potential downstream billing/priority analytics skew for mid-market customers using cohort-based SLA routing.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (orchestrator v1.4.3, reporting-aggregator v2.1.0, template-compiler v0.9.8)
- Affected service: orchestrator serializer (hosted in k8s cluster cluster-orch-01) and reporting aggregation worker (batch-runner-07).

Observed behavior:
- Serialization output contains keys like "tmp_cohort:enterprise_42" instead of canonical "enterprise_42".
- Aggregator treats unknown prefix as new bucket and does not remap during aggregation window.
- Graphs on the SLA dashboard show sudden drop in counts for known cohorts and growth in "(unknown)" bucket.

Expected behavior:
- Serializer should emit canonical cohort identifiers consistently. Aggregator should either normalize known prefixes or drop malformed cohort keys and surface errors for remediation.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) On cluster-orch-01, run a dry-serialize using the current orchestrator binary against a recent routing snapshot: 
   kubectl exec -n infra orchestrator-0 -- /app/bin/orch --dry-serialize --snapshot-id=2026-02-27
2) Inspect the output payloads in /tmp/serialization-dump/*.json and grep for "tmp_cohort:" prefix.
3) Run local copy of reporting-aggregator v2.1.0 against the dump and observe separate buckets in the aggregation output.

Logs / evidence:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/SLAs/sla-cohort-overview?orgId=1&from=1646000000000&to=1646604800000
- Orchestrator logs (sample): "WARN serializer - emitted unknown cohort prefix=tmp_cohort enterprise_42" (link to log slice: https://logs.redwood.ai/orch/2026-03-01/serializer-logs.gz)
- Aggregator run metadata: batch-run-07 job id 2026-02-28-agg-71 shows "unclassified_cohorts=1354"

Business/operational notes:
This began to surface after a canary build of orchestrator was promoted to stable on 2026-02-26 (v1.4.3). The serializer binary includes a new temporary-cohort feature intended for in-progress migrations; it was supposed to set a compatibility flag but that flag was not respected when the binary ran in prod. The issue has exposure to enterprise-tier routing and weekly SLAs for multiple accounts.

2026-03-01 11:05 - Oncall (Marco Alvarez): Reproduced dry-serialize locally, seeing tmp_cohort prefixes. Opening investigation; suspect serializer drift between v1.4.2 and v1.4.3. Correlating with recent canary promotion.

Aggregator hotfix (reporting v2.1.1) deployed to ignore unknown prefixes when seen in historical windows. Backfill completed and exec report re-generated. Marking as In Progress while we monitor 48h telemetry.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: backward-incompatible flag in serializer binary introduced a transient prefix for cohorts. Evidence: 1) deployment timeline matches spike in unclassified cohorts; 2) dry-serialize output contains "tmp_cohort:" prefix only from v1.4.3 nodes; 3) aggregator has no normalization path for that prefix. Queries run: SELECT count(*) FROM routing_snapshot WHERE cohort LIKE 'tmp_cohort:%' (result 1,354) and checked job metadata for batch-run-07; memory footprint unchanged. Root cause appears to be a config gating error in the orchestrator promote job where COMPAT_COHORT_FLAG was not set.

Technical findings:
- Orchestrator v1.4.3 binary changed serializer behavior when env var COHORT_MIGRATION_MODE=staged but the promote job did not set COHORT_MIGRATION_MODE=compat.
- Serializer emits a header X-Serializer-Compat; v1.4.3 omitted it in the production docker image build step due to a Dockerfile ARG mismatch.
- Aggregator assumed any unknown cohort string is a newly created cohort and increments unclassified counters instead of dropping or normalizing.
action_items: Short-term: Deploy serializer v1.4.4 with compatibility enforcement to prod-us-east (done 2026-03-05).
Short-term: Add transient normalization mapping tmp_cohort:* -> * in routing-indexer (applied 2026-03-02).
Mid-term: Backfill aggregator data for 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-28 and regenerate executive weekly report (completed 2026-03-03).
Mid-term: Add unit/integration test in release pipeline to ensure X-Serializer-Compat header present for production images (work tracked in GH PR 477).
Long-term: Add guardrail in deploy pipeline to fail promotion if serializer flag mismatch detected; document migration gating in Confluence.
resolution: Partial remediation applied. Serializer rolled to v1.4.4 with compatibility enforcement and aggregator patched (v2.1.1) to ignore malformed prefix when seen in historical windows. Backfill job executed and weekly report re-generated; counts reconciled and exec dashboard updated with a note about the corrective action. Monitoring placed to watch unclassified_cohorts metric for 7 days. Follow-up ticket created to harden release gating (INT-789101).
